prompt: Why is every problem in NP also in PSPACE?

options.text: Because NP problems can be solved in polynomial time
options.explanation: That's the open P vs NP question. Nobody knows NP problems can be solved in polynomial time.

options.text: Because a polynomial-space machine can try every certificate in turn, reusing the same polynomial space for each check
options.explanation: Correct. Exponentially many certificates take exponential time, but each check needs only polynomial space, which is wiped and reused.
PSPACE allows only polynomial space. That's EXPSPACE.

options.text: It isn't known; NP vs PSPACE is open
options.explanation: Whether NP equals PSPACE is open, but the inclusion of NP in PSPACE is proven.

workedExample: Enumerate one polynomial-length certificate at a time. Run its polynomial-time verifier, then reuse the same storage for the next candidate. The number of trials can be exponential, but memory holds only the current certificate, the counter and one verifier run. That gives polynomial space without a polynomial-time claim.

prompt: A deterministic machine on a fixed input returns to exactly the same control state, head positions and work-tape contents before halting. What follows?

options.text: It may halt later because it has used more time
options.explanation: Elapsed time is not extra machine state unless stored; the identical state has the identical next step.

options.text: It will repeat the same future forever
options.explanation: Determinism makes a repeated complete configuration an infinite cycle.

options.text: It must have used more memory than permitted
options.explanation: A cycle can occur within a tiny fixed workspace.

options.text: The same conclusion holds for every nondeterministic branch choice
options.explanation: A nondeterministic computation may take a different outgoing choice on a later visit; the deterministic argument does not apply unchanged.

workedExample: A full configuration includes the state, head positions and work-tape contents on the fixed input. Determinism makes the next configuration fixed. Revisiting one therefore repeats the same future forever; a later halt cannot suddenly appear. Counting configurations bounds the length of any halting deterministic run, but counting only tape contents would miss part of the state.
